title: Sapiom template manifest
description: Rich per-template detail, co-located beside each example as `template.json`. The registry (`registry.json`) stays the thin gallery list (id/name/description/tags/sourcePath/capabilities/steps); this manifest is the detail layer the Sapiom backend merges into the template + fork detail view. Everything is optional except `manifestVersion` — a bare `{ "manifestVersion": 1 }` is valid.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint pointing at this schema for autocomplete + validation.

manifestVersion.description: Manifest schema version. Only `1` is defined today.

url.description: Optional link to the author (site, profile, or repo).

longDescription.description: Markdown prose describing what the template is and how it behaves. Shown on the detail view.

useCases.description: Short phrases describing concrete things you'd use this template for.

notes.description: Markdown notes — how to use it, what else it ships with, gotchas.

examples.description: Sample runs: an input, and optionally the output it produces.

requiredSecrets.description: Third-party credentials the template needs. ONLY for credentials Sapiom cannot broker — never a Sapiom API key, never a non-secret value (use `settings`). Declares what the credential IS, never where it is stored: there is no `vaultRef`, no `connectorId`, no `store`, and there never will be. Binding `key` to a concrete value belongs to the resolver (`process.env[key]` today), which is what lets resolution move to connectors later without touching a manifest or the deploy panel.

key.description: Logical identifier the run reads. Must satisfy the engine's process-env rules: cannot be PATH, SAPIOM_*, or WORKFLOWS_* — namespace rules this pattern cannot express, enforced by the `manifest-secret-key` check in examples-check.

label.description: Human label for the input field.

provider.description: Provider hint (e.g. "slack", "notion"). NOT a storage location.

credentialKind.description: Shape of the credential, so the panel can label and validate the field.

description.description: Helper text: what it is, where to get it.

docsUrl.description: Link to the third party's token-creation page.

optional.description: True when the template degrades honestly without it — the run still reaches a terminal state and names what it skipped in `unmet[]`. False means the run cannot do its job at all.

settings.description: Non-secret configuration with a declared default, rendered as ordinary form fields and merged into the run input. Where a RECIPIENT or a lookback window belongs — NOT the vault, which cannot be listed, validated, or prompted for.

path.description: Dotted path into the entry-step input object this setting fills (e.g. `deliverTo`, `client.email`).

label.description: Human label for the form field.

description.description: Helper text shown under the field.

default.description: The value used when the user supplies nothing. REQUIRED — a setting without a default cannot support a zero-interaction run, which is the entire point.

example.description: A realistic value shown as placeholder text.

defaultInput.description: The input a zero-interaction run starts with. Merged UNDER the user's input and UNDER `settings` defaults, so an explicit value always wins. Distinct from `examples[0].input`, which is documentation and may legitimately contain values that cannot work on a fresh tenant (a repo slug, a live sandbox URL). The runtime guarantee lives in code (`z.string().min(1).default("Sapiom")`); this is its declared, renderable projection — the UI cannot introspect a zod schema across a GitHub fetch — and it NEVER overrides code.

zeroSetup.description: The machine-checkable expectation for an unconfigured run. An expectation asserts that the pattern demonstrably ran and the output is honest about it — not that the result is production-grade.

terminalState.description: The terminal state a zero-input, zero-credential run is expected to reach.

expect.description: Assertions over the terminal artifact that prove the pattern ran.

path.description: Dotted path into the terminal artifact.

assert.description: Closed assertion vocabulary — anything outside it is a check failure, not a new operator.

narrative.description: One honest sentence for what an unconfigured run actually produces. Rendered VERBATIM on the shelf as `setup.degradedWithoutSetup` — must never imply a send that will not happen.
